subject: Chemistry
title: d- and f-Block Elements
summary: Transition (d-block) elements have partly filled d orbitals in the atom or a common ion: configuration (n − 1)d¹⁻¹⁰ ns¹⁻². Zn, Cd and Hg (d¹⁰ in all states) are not counted as true transition elements.

Typical properties: high melting points (strong metallic bonding from d electrons), variable oxidation states, coloured ions (d–d transitions), paramagnetism (unpaired electrons), catalytic activity, complex formation, interstitial compounds and alloys.
KMnO₄ and K₂Cr₂O₇ are the two key compounds: strong oxidising agents whose preparation, structure and reactions are frequently asked.
Lanthanoids (4f) mostly show +3; lanthanoid contraction makes 4d and 5d elements of a group (Zr–Hf) almost the same size. Actinoids (5f) are radioactive and show more oxidation states.

formulas.name: General configuration
formulas.note: Cr = [Ar]3d⁵4s¹ and Cu = [Ar]3d¹⁰4s¹ (extra stability of half/fully filled d).

formulas.name: Spin-only magnetic moment
formulas.note: Count unpaired d electrons of the ION, after removing 4s electrons first.

formulas.name: Oxidation states
formulas.formula: maximum = (n − 1)d + ns electrons up to Mn (+7);  Sc only +3;  Zn only +2;  common for many: +2 and +3

formulas.name: Colour
formulas.formula: arises from d–d transitions; d⁰ (Sc³⁺, Ti⁴⁺) and d¹⁰ (Zn²⁺, Cu⁺) ions are colourless

formulas.name: E° and stability
formulas.formula: E°(M²⁺/M) mostly negative;  Cu has positive E° (+0.34 V) — doesn't liberate H₂ from acids;  Mn²⁺ (d⁵) and Zn²⁺ (d¹⁰) are especially stable

formulas.name: KMnO₄ in acid
formulas.note: In neutral/weakly alkaline medium MnO₄⁻ → MnO₂ (3e⁻); in strongly alkaline → MnO₄²⁻ (1e⁻).

formulas.name: Chromate–dichromate equilibrium
formulas.mistake: Cr stays +6 — it is an acid–base change, not redox.

formulas.name: Preparation of KMnO₄
formulas.formula: MnO₂ fused with KOH + O₂ → K₂MnO₄ (green manganate) → disproportionation/electrolytic oxidation → KMnO₄ (purple)

formulas.name: Preparation of K₂Cr₂O₇
formulas.formula: chromite ore FeCr₂O₄ + Na₂CO₃ + O₂ → Na₂CrO₄ → (H⁺) Na₂Cr₂O₇ → (KCl) K₂Cr₂O₇

formulas.name: Lanthanoid contraction
formulas.formula: steady decrease in size from La to Lu due to poor shielding by 4f electrons
formulas.when: Why Zr and Hf have nearly equal radii and similar chemistry.
formulas.note: Basicity of Ln(OH)₃ decreases from La(OH)₃ to Lu(OH)₃.

formulas.name: Lanthanoid oxidation states
formulas.formula: +3 common;  Ce⁴⁺ strong oxidant (→ Ce³⁺);  Eu²⁺, Yb²⁺ reductants (→ +3)

examples.title: Electrons in KMnO₄ reduction
examples.problem: How many moles of Fe²⁺ does 1 mol of KMnO₄ oxidise in acid?
examples.solution: MnO₄⁻ gains 5 electrons (+7 → +2); each Fe²⁺ loses 1 → 5 mol Fe²⁺.

examples.title: Electrons for dichromate
examples.problem: Electrons needed to reduce one Cr₂O₇²⁻ to Cr³⁺?

examples.title: Colourless ions
examples.problem: Which is colourless: Sc³⁺, Ti³⁺, Cu²⁺, Mn²⁺?
examples.solution: Sc³⁺ — it is 3d⁰, so no d–d transition is possible.

examples.title: Copper and acids
examples.problem: Why doesn't copper liberate hydrogen from dilute HCl?
examples.solution: E°(Cu²⁺/Cu) = +0.34 V is positive, so Cu cannot reduce H⁺ to H₂. Copper dissolves only in oxidising acids like HNO₃.

topics.title: Position and classification
topics.explain: d-block: groups 3–12 in periods 4–7 (3d, 4d, 5d, 6d series). f-block: lanthanoids (Ce–Lu, 4f) and actinoids (Th–Lr, 5f), placed separately below the table.

topics.title: Physical properties
topics.explain: Hard, high melting and boiling points, good conductors. Melting point peaks in the middle of the series (more unpaired d electrons, stronger bonding); Mn and Zn are anomalously low. Atomic radii change little across the series.

topics.title: Ionisation enthalpies and oxidation states
topics.explain: IE rises slowly across the series. The number of oxidation states rises up to Mn (+2 to +7) then falls. Higher states are stabilised by O and F (MnO₄⁻, CrO₃, VF₅).

topics.title: Catalytic properties
topics.explain: Variable oxidation states and the ability to adsorb reactants make transition metals good catalysts: V₂O₅ (contact process), Fe (Haber process), Ni (hydrogenation), MnO₂ (decomposition of KClO₃).

topics.title: Interstitial compounds and alloys
topics.explain: Small atoms (H, C, N) fit in metal lattices, making them hard and high-melting (steel, TiC). Similar atomic sizes let transition metals form alloys like brass (Cu–Zn) and bronze (Cu–Sn).

topics.title: Lanthanoids
topics.explain: Show mainly +3, form coloured ions (except La³⁺, Lu³⁺), are reactive metals, and their hydroxides become less basic across the series. Mischmetal (a lanthanoid alloy) is used in lighter flints.

topics.title: Actinoids and comparison
topics.explain: All actinoids are radioactive. They show a wider range of oxidation states (up to +7) because 5f, 6d and 7s energies are close. Actinoid contraction is greater than lanthanoid contraction because 5f electrons shield even more poorly.

ratta: Mn shows max +7;  Sc only +3;  Zn only +2.
CrO₄²⁻ yellow ⇌ Cr₂O₇²⁻ orange (pH, not redox).
